subject: NordicBank private deployment onboarding, handover & procurement
messages:
From: Elaine Hansen <elaine.hansen@nordicbank.no>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Pettersen <m.pettersen@nordicbank.no>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:12:00 +0200
Subject: Private deploy - onboarding scope and timeline

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are ready to move forward with a private deployment of Redwood in two controlled regions: EU (Norway/EU data residency) and APAC (Singapore-only residency for a subset of workloads). Before procurement we need a clear onboarding/handover checklist and a concrete timeline that shows:

- Which components must remain in-region (KV cache, model weights, audit logs)
- Network topology and peering requirements for our on-prem racks to talk to Redwood control plane (we prefer minimal egress and private peering)
- Expected downtime/RTO for regional failover tests and whether cross-border cache fetch is acceptable during drills
- Procurement items (HW SKU list, estimated DC rack count, and any 3rd-party network appliance recommendations)

Can you share a single doc that ties the topology to procurement timeline and any SLA exceptions we should request? We also need to know signoff steps from your side (who will be looped in for acceptance).

Regards,
Elaine Hansen
Head of Cloud Architecture | NordicBank ASA

--
Attachment: none (we'll upload PO when we confirm scope)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Hansen <elaine.hansen@nordicbank.no>
Cc: Markus Pettersen <m.pettersen@nordicbank.no>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 11:05:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy - onboarding scope and timeline

Hi Elaine,

Appreciate the clear asks — I attached a compact package that should map to everything you listed. High level summary here:

1) Topology & in-region constraints\  - Model weights, primary KV stores, and audit logs are required to remain in-region by default. Control plane metadata (non-sensitive) can be in Redwood control plane with in-region encryption keys.

2) Failover model\  - We recommend warm-standby in APAC for latency-sensitive workloads and cold standby for batch-only workloads. During scheduled failover drills we allow read-only cross-region cache fill for 30 minutes (configurable) to keep RTO under 10 minutes for session handoff tests.

3) Network requirements\  - Minimal outbound connectivity from your DCs to our control-plane endpoints over TLS (mTLS option available). For lower-latency paths we support private VPC peering with BGP (we provided port and prefix guidance in the attached text file).

4) Procurement items + timeline\  - Attached PO timeline (sheet 1) and a recommended HW SKU list (sheet 2). Short summary: 2 GPU racks per region for initial capacity; add 1 rack per additional 20 qps sustained.

5) Acceptance & signoffs\  - Onboarding acceptance requires: (a) network connectivity validated, (b) canary run (30k tokens/day) for 3 days with <50ms P50 on EU region, (c) audit log ingestion verified. We'll designate a solutions engineer and an ops point for the handover; Lauren will be your primary contact for the canary acceptance.

Next steps: I'll kick off a call to walk the topology later today. Attaching: residency-topology-v1.pdf, canary-runbook.xlsx, po-timeline.xlsx.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: residency-topology-v1.pdf (21 pages), canary-runbook.xlsx (3 sheets), po-timeline.xlsx

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Elaine Hansen <elaine.hansen@nordicbank.no>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Markus Pettersen <m.pettersen@nordicbank.no>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 13:18:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy - onboarding scope and timeline

Thanks Marissa — couple of clarifications from an acceptance/SLA perspective before we lock the procurement timeline:

- Legal asks that any customer-requested cross-border failover (i.e., failing EU -> APAC) be handled as an SLA exception and documented in the SOW. If NordicBank wants automatic cross-border failover with stateful KV mirroring, we need a signed SLA exception.

- KMS: For EU-residency of keys, we require either (a) customer-managed KMS in-region with HSM-backed keys or (b) Redwood-managed KMS with dedicated key isolation — legal prefers (a) for banks. We'll need your KMS admin contact.

- Audit evidence: ops will provide time-bound proofs of residency (signed logs) during handover. For long-term retention differences across regions (EU vs SG), we should add a short clause indicating retention windows and export controls.

If you can confirm the KMS approach and whether you want cross-border stateful mirroring we can finalize the SOW and push the PO date out by 2 business days for final signoff.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Product Ops | Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Elaine Hansen <elaine.hansen@nordicbank.no>
Cc: Markus Pettersen <m.pettersen@nordicbank.no>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 09:36:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy - onboarding scope and timeline

Bringing in ops detail + minimal config we need from NordicBank for a clean handover:

Network and peering checklist (high level):
- Public control-plane endpoints: outbound HTTPS over 443 to endpoints in eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1. For private peering provide a BGP session + two /30s for BFD.
- ASN and prefix ranges: please pick non-overlapping RFC1918 ranges for each region; our preferred ranges are in the attached network-acls.txt.
- Firewall & egress: allow 443/TCP to control-plane FQDNs; restrict IP ranges to the two announced prefixes.
- MTLS: we will onboard your device cert (PEM) and require mTLS for administrative APIs.

Operational requirements:
- Time sync (NTP) must be accurate to <100ms for audit log correlation.
- Proof-of-residency: ops will run a signed fetcher that emits signed manifests every 24h to an in-region S3 bucket (we'll provide the lambda).
- Failover behavior: for warm-standby we replicate KV snapshot every 15 minutes; for cross-region stateful mirroring add an additional 4-6% bandwidth overhead during steady state.

Attachments: network-acls.txt (recommended CIDR/AWS peering examples).

I'll coordinate a short tech call with your network team to pin down the BGP and NAT behavior.

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni
Principal SRE | Redwood Inference

From: Markus Pettersen <m.pettersen@nordicbank.no>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elaine Hansen <elaine.hansen@nordicbank.no>, Tom Baker <tom.baker@cloudzone.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 15:47:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy - onboarding scope and timeline

Thanks team — this is very helpful. A few operational notes from procurement/legal:

- Procurement: PO ready target is 2027-08-05 pending final SOW. I attached our internal PO tracker but I will upload the formal PO after we sign the SOW.
- KMS: we will use our in-region HSM-backed KMS for EU (Norway) and a separate KMS instance in SG. KMS admin is Elaine (cc'd).
- SLAs: we will request that cross-border stateful mirroring be an opt-in addendum in the SOW. Otherwise, warm-standby plan as described is acceptable.

Action items:
1) Lauren to draft the short SOW addendum for cross-border failover options and call out SLA exception process.
2) Vivek to schedule a 30-min network scoping call with our network team next Wed (time tbd).
3) Marissa to share revised topology with a single sheet that maps each procurement SKU to the acceptance criteria.

Tom from CloudZone — can you confirm estimated transit appliance lead times for Singapore racks (we may need 4-6 weeks depending on model)?

I'll sign the SOW once the addendum is finalized.

Best,
Markus Pettersen
Sourcing Manager | NordicBank ASA

--
Attachment: po-timeline.xlsx (internal tracker sheet)
